layer_status.detail: Both per-view files are pure re-export shims over createViewInteractionRegistry(viewName). Verified line by line: identical modulo the literal "week"/"day" argument and export identifiers. No logic in either.

Note both WeekGridEventTargetType and DayGridEventTargetType resolve to the SAME type ViewInteractionEventType = "all-day" | "timed", so the generic parameter buys nothing today. Only real difference is a gratuitous formatting variance in the Day generic call.
layer_status.recommendation: Leave as-is. Optional: drop the redundant type aliases.

layer_status.detail: Eight interface pairs (AllDayDrag/AllDayResize/TimedDrag/TimedResize x Target/CommitResult) are structurally identical after name normalization. The four commit-result shapes are byte-identical modulo the Week/Day prefix. Genuine divergence is confined to: Options (Day adds getColumnKeys/getVisibleDate and uses shared GridLayoutCacheSources; Week uses its own WeekLayoutCacheSources), Runtime (Week adds getVisibleDays + onRequestWeekNavigation), Adapter (Week adds rebuildLayoutAfterNavigation), and Week-only WeekEdgeNavigableVisual.
layer_status.recommendation: Best first target. A generic ViewInteractionTypes<TColumnKey, TRuntimeExtras> factory collapses ~110 of 149 lines per file with no runtime risk.

layer_status.detail: Both export a single create*InteractionAdapter factory implementing the same InteractionAdapter contract. Week is decomposed into adapter/interactions/{all-day.drag,all-day.resize,all-day.visible-range,timed.drag,timed.resize}.ts (5 modules, 385 LOC total); Day is monolithic. Roughly 40 percent of the normalized delta is Week-only capability (edge navigation, cross-row drag, layout rebuild), not divergent copies of shared logic.
layer_status.divergence_note: My normalized diff is 408 lines vs the prior run's 448; same ballpark, different normalizer. Both agree the adapter is the bulk of the work and is NOT a clean copy-paste pair.
layer_status.recommendation: Unify toward Week's decomposed shape, not Day's monolith. Sequence this AFTER the type work.

layer_status.detail: Independently re-derived and CONFIRMED. Two orthogonal differences. (1) Shape: Week exports pure visual->GridEvent transforms and lets the adapter wrap them; Day exports whole commit functions returning a full CommitResult. (2) Semantics: in Week a column is a DAY, in Day a column is a CALENDAR. Week all-day drag applies a day delta to startDate/endDate; Day all-day drag deliberately does NOT touch dates (documented: rewriting to visible date would truncate a multi-day all-day event) and instead sets calendarId. Day timed drag pins dates to visibleDate and moves calendarId.
layer_status.recommendation: Do NOT merge commit bodies. At most unify the CommitResult envelope shape (Day's) and keep per-view transforms.

layer_status.disagreement: The prior run filed geometry under 'Genuinely duplicated - the real targets' and described the pair as both wrapping the same builders with the same constants, differing only in edge-threshold source and extra input. I disagree: after name normalization essentially every line differs. They share DEPENDENCIES (same shared builders, same ID_* and GRID_* constants), not STRUCTURE.
structural_differences: Week funnels everything through one weekLayoutCacheOptions(sources) builder then exposes 3 thin wrappers; Day writes two independent option literals that duplicate each other internally.
Week exposes buildDragWeekLayoutCache (both rows at once, for cross-row drag). Day has NO cross-row builder at all.
Edge threshold: Week uses WEEK_EDGE_NAVIGATION_THRESHOLD_PX; Day uses INTERACTION_EDGE_THRESHOLD_PX for timed and hardcoded 0 for all-day.
Day's file additionally hosts adapter concerns: buildDayLayoutCacheForTarget, isAllDayTarget, isDayDragTarget. Week keeps the equivalent predicates private inside its adapter (lines 755-760).
layer_status.recommendation: Lower unification value than prior run implied. Real win is smaller: hoist the shared option-literal into one builder and move Day's target predicates out of the geometry file.

type_safety_hazards.title: Column-key overload: dayDate/initialDayDate mean different things per view, both typed string
type_safety_hazards.prior_run_flagged: partially - prior run named only TimedDragVisual.dayDate
type_safety_hazards.my_characterization: The overload spans FOUR fields across TWO shared types, not one. All four are plain `string`.
type_safety_hazards.producer: Week passes YYYY-MM-DD dates. Day passes CALENDAR IDS - see day-interaction.adapter.ts lines 254-282 and 313, where columnKeys come from getColumnKeys() (calendar ids) and initialColumnKey is fed to createTimedDragVisual/createAllDayDragVisual as dayDate. The shared factories at grid/interaction/math/timed.drag.ts:48 and math/all-day.drag.ts:35 then set `initialDayDate: dayDate`, propagating the same overload to the initial field.
type_safety_hazards.unchecked_assertion: views/Day/interaction/adapter/commit/timed.commit.ts:78-83 columnMoveCalendarId does `visual.dayDate as CalendarId` - an unchecked cast that the compiler cannot validate.
type_safety_hazards.failure_mode: If a unified engine routes Day visuals through Week's date-parsing commit path, dayjs('<calendarId>') yields Invalid Date, diff() yields NaN, and event dates silently corrupt. TypeScript catches nothing because every field is `string`.
doc_rot: TimedDragVisual.initialDayDate docstring still says 'Local YYYY-MM-DD date of the source column at drag start.' - wrong for Day view.
AllDayDragVisual.initialDayDate docstring says 'Local YYYY-MM-DD date of the (window-clamped) source column' - wrong for Day view.

AllDayDragVisual.dayDate carries TWO stacked block comments (lines 15-27); the first describes it as a date and is stale, the second correctly notes the per-view overload. Contradictory docs on one field.
type_safety_hazards.mitigation: Introduce a branded/parameterised column-key type (TColumnKey generic, or DateColumnKey | CalendarColumnKey brands) and thread it through TimedDragVisual/AllDayDragVisual BEFORE merging any commit or adapter logic. This is exactly what the prior run's shipped commit 62162a95 did, and it is the correct first move.
type_safety_hazards.gate_recommendation: Treat as a hard sequencing constraint: no commit-layer or adapter-layer merge lands before H1 is fixed.

type_safety_hazards.title: Week-shaped fields on the shared visual types are dead weight in Day
type_safety_hazards.detail: TimedDragVisual.row, TimedDragVisual.crossRowSize, AllDayDragVisual.row, AllDayDragVisual.crossRowSize and AllDayDragVisual.timedStartMinutes exist on the shared types but only Week ever drives them - Day has no cross-row drag. A naive unification will make Day appear to support cross-row drops because the fields typecheck, while nothing populates them.
type_safety_hazards.mitigation: Either make cross-row capability part of the parameterised visual type, or explicitly document Day as opting out.

type_safety_hazards.title: Redundant per-view target-type aliases
type_safety_hazards.detail: WeekGridEventTargetType and DayGridEventTargetType are both aliases of ViewInteractionEventType ('all-day' | 'timed'). The generic parameter on createGridEventTargeting is unused in practice - both instantiations pass the same type.

blast_radius.fragile_public_surface: grid/interaction/view-event-registry.ts exports CALENDAR_VIEW_INTERACTION_ID_ATTRIBUTES, calendarEventIdElementSelector, calendarEventIdValueSelector and readCalendarEventIdFromElement. These resolve an event id from the DOM without knowing the view and are used by context menus and undo focus-restore. Renaming the data-${view}-interaction-event-* attribute scheme breaks them.

src_interaction.role: View-agnostic pointer-interaction engine. Fully generic already.
src_interaction.stops_at: Knows nothing about grids, columns, dates or calendars. Owns pointer lifecycle, draft-event DOM cloning, cursor lock, source-element visibility and the PointerCaptureBoundary React wrapper.
src_interaction.contract_note: updateVisual is documented as MUST BE IDEMPOTENT - the engine re-invokes it at pointerup with the same pointer before commit. Any refactor must preserve this.

grid_interaction.stops_at: It does NOT provide an adapter factory. Each view hand-assembles its own createXInteractionAdapter over the engine. That gap - not the engine - is the actual duplication surface.
grid_interaction.recommended_direction: Widen grid/interaction/ with a view-parameterised adapter factory (createGridInteractionAdapter<TColumnKey, ...>). Do NOT push Week/Day grid logic down into src/interaction/, which must stay grid-agnostic.

recommended_sequencing: 1. Fix H1: brand/parameterise the column key across TimedDragVisual and AllDayDragVisual (all four fields) and correct the three stale docstrings. Type-only, no behavior change.
2. Unify adapter.types via a generic factory (~110 of 149 lines per file).
3. Extract the shared coordinator lifecycle hook.
4. Hoist the geometry option-literal; move Day's target predicates out of the geometry file.
5. Only then consider an adapter factory in grid/interaction, unifying toward Week's decomposed interactions/ shape.
NOT recommended: merging commit bodies (divergent by design), collapsing registry/targeting shims (already unified).
